plan: My value for the prize is $31. To maximize profit, I should bid slightly above the average expected value of the other bidders. Given values are uniformly drawn between $0 and $49, the average is $24.5. To win and maximize profit, I'll bid slightly above this, considering the third-highest bid will likely be lower. I'll bid $27 to balance the chance of winning and the payment if I win.

Given my private value of $37, I aim to bid below my value to ensure a profit if I win. Since the prize value is randomly drawn and bids are in $0.1 increments, I will bid $30. This bid maximizes potential profit while considering the risk of overbidding. If I win, I pay the third-highest bid, ideally less than $30, ensuring profit. If others bid higher, I retain my endowment.

Given my value of $11, I should bid conservatively to ensure I do not overpay. Since the value is low, I will bid slightly below my value to avoid paying more than what the prize is worth to me. This minimizes potential losses if I win. I will bid $10, which is slightly under my value, to potentially win if other bidders undervalue their bids.
